Oct 26
kevin peach
Basis for the week
We have been talking a lot on the market looking for demand and it’s exactly what is happening. Basis and futures both weak on corn and beans as SAM sold all the Oct-Jan corn as US futures ran up. Beans China is a smaller PNW buyer than market thought and selling a bean train Oct-Dec next to impossible. Corn same for the most part. We need to see demand or basis snuggles more. We are out of harms way and will now dump and ship. Open today 8-7 in line by 6.30. Sunday 12-7 in line by 6.30. Monday we start to pile.

kevin peach
USDA reports
Traders have opinions as does everyone. Be careful on opinions. I am asked often my thoughts on reports but the one who has all the tools is USDA and is why they drive the market. We watch what demand does on rallies and price drops as that is a great opinion. As a producer you have to to look when cash needs are, profit levels are, when can you haul, carries etc and lock in prices. We do not sell when we know very bullish items but even then have a finger on avg sell button. Just a thought on USDA reports. We did see some nibbles on corn and beans on this price drop.If you are a Co-op customer and want our paid for Van Trump report call me or Chris. I really like his way of selling and reporting.

Post report
After reading a lot of info USDA in the past is very slow to adjust yield data from Oct very quickly. Funds are long which in beans and corn is a risk of them selling. We are well sold but we would suggest to raise cash sell all the beans. Hold wheat thats left. And keep corn for a better basis and carry. Just a thought. Open today for beans only 12-7 All stations. Call 218-791-5769 for hedging tonight.

Markets
Markets are waiting on US/China meeting. Corn and wheat are overpriced in the world extra volume side that Russia/Ukraine cannot fill. Its going to SAM and Canada. So extra corn and wheat sales to China needs to happen for another leg higher. Otherwise the market seems tired. Listen to the Van Trump news letter this am if you get it. Its a great read or listen.

Todays markets
Markets slip a little as so much world pressure to end the wars comes at UN. In corn and wheat we priced ourselves out of the world market on last run up so a lot hinges on US/China making a sweat ag deal. New crop sales are slow for wheat and corn. Most recent bean sales have been sold out of the gulf due to short northern crop and ample sellers in mid west and east that ship on the rivers. No wheat at H as we are doing a main house repair. Open 8-7
